title: Roman and Reformed — election/praedestinatio not used the same way
source_text: XXIX. Porro ex dictis patet voces electionis & praedestinationis, tam in communione Romana quam Reformata, non eodem modo & sensu usurpari: & varias esse vocum illarum acceptiones apud utriusque Scholae Theologos. Verum tamen quosdam esse vocum istarum usus in Schola Romana plurimum receptos, quos non admittit Schola Reformata, & vicissim voces illas a multis Reformatis usurpari eo sensu qui non habet locum in Schola Romana.
pass_a_gloss: Further from what has been said it is plain that the words election and predestination, both in the Roman communion and in the Reformed, are not used in the same mode and sense: and that there are various acceptations of those words among the Theologians of either School. Yet it is true that there are certain uses of those words most received in the Roman School which the Reformed School does not admit, and conversely that those words are used by many of the Reformed in a sense which has no place in the Roman School.
pass_b_english: Both communions use electio / praedestinatio — not in one shared sense.
Some Roman uses Reformed refuse; some Reformed senses have no place at Rome.
